The Question on Reconnection "Venerable sir, when a man has committed an evil deed, does that evil deed immediately follow him, or does it follow him after some time? "It is not immediately, great king, that the evil deed follows him; rather, it follows him after some time. "But, venerable sir, what is the reason for this? What is the cause for this? "The evil deed, great king, is heavy with defilement, and it is because of its being heavy with defilement that it does not immediately follow him. However, as time passes, the defilements gradually diminish, and when they have diminished, the evil deed follows him. "Venerable sir, if the evil deed does not immediately follow him, but follows him after some time, then surely there is no point in guarding oneself against evil deeds? "There is a point, great king, in guarding oneself against evil deeds. For even though the evil deed does not immediately follow him, it will follow him after some time. Therefore, one should guard oneself against evil deeds. "Venerable sir, how is it that the evil deed follows him after some time? "Suppose, great king, a man were to throw a stone or a clod of earth upwards. Would that stone or clod of earth immediately fall back down to the ground? "No, venerable sir. It would fall back down to the ground after some time. "In the same way, great king, the evil deed does not immediately follow him; rather, it follows him after some time. Therefore, one should guard oneself against evil deeds. "Venerable sir, how is it that the evil deed follows him after some time? "Suppose, great king, a man were to plant a seed in the earth. Would that seed immediately sprout? "No, venerable sir. It would sprout after some time. "In the same way, great king, the evil deed does not immediately follow him; rather, it follows him after some time. Therefore, one should guard oneself against evil deeds. "Venerable sir, how is it that the evil deed follows him after some time? "Suppose, great king, a man were to strike a drum with a drumstick. Would the sound immediately cease? "No, venerable sir. "Venerable Nāgasena, does he who does not undergo rebirth know, 'I shall not undergo rebirth'?
"Yes, Great King, he who does not undergo rebirth knows, 'I shall not undergo rebirth.'"
“How does he know this, venerable sir?
“By whatever cause and by whatever condition there is rebirth-linking, O Great King, through the cessation of that cause and that condition, he knows: ‘I shall not be reborn.
“Just as, great king, a farmer householder, having ploughed and sown,
might fill his granary; and at a later time, he would neither plough nor sow, but would consume the grain already gathered,
or distribute it, or use it for whatever purpose was required— would that farmer householder, great king, know [this]?”
“‘My granary will not be filled,’ would you know that?
“Yes, venerable sir, I would know it.
“Just as one who knows the cause and the condition for the filling of a granary understands, upon the cessation of that cause and that condition,
‘My granary will not be filled,’ even so, Great King, one who knows the cause and the condition for rebirth understands, upon the cessation of that cause and that condition,
‘I shall not be reborn. “You are clever, Bhante Nāgasena.”
